traits: Cap 4 to 20 cm, tan to dark brown, smooth or velvety, sticky when wet
Pores whitish then grey, browning when touched
Stem 5 to 20 cm, white, covered in small blackish-brown scales
Whitish flesh, almost unchanging when cut; mild taste, faint smell
Almost only under birch · summer to late autumn
safetyNote: Edible when well cooked: the DGfM and the VAPKO list the rough-stemmed boletes, and Wikipedia (fr) warns that raw or undercooked ones cause digestive upset. Of medium value; the fibrous stem is often thrown away, young caps are preferred. The flesh darkens, even turns black, when cooked (Wikipedia, fr and en). The many other rough-stemmed boletes are close; the sources read give no simple rule to separate them.

sources.title: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Mykologie (DGfM), Fachausschuss Pilzverwertung und Toxikologie (2026). Positivliste der Speisepilze, Stand 1. Mai 2026.
